answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity stake reputation that is costly to rebuild: before trading, an agent locks a small bond and completes verifiable work peers attest to, so one operator spinning up many fake identities pays the price each time. Like a dune that shifts yet keeps its shape, the network weights trust by sustained history, not raw count. A lotus pattern helps too — new identities with no roots earn little weight until they show useful behavior. An onyx ledger keeps the record tamper-evident, so sybil clusters copying each other's claims stand out and get down-weighted.
